analysis: The hypothesis is refuted under the tested configuration. The censored watch-time auxiliary produced a trusted primary delta of -0.001229 versus the incumbent, with a paired 95% CI of [-0.002228, -0.000172], excluding zero. Per-seed comparison was also consistently negative (-0.002207; CI [-0.003003, -0.001305]). Diagnostic slices show no clear compensating segment: all user-history quartiles, all item-popularity quartiles, and every reported tab declined, with especially large degradation for the least-popular item quartile (-0.004046) and tabs 0, 2, and 6. The intended portfolio diversification benefit was not demonstrated either: replacing a portfolio member yielded -0.000253, with a CI crossing zero, so the candidate was not promoted. These results establish that adding this watch head at fixed weight 0.2 to the reproduced pointwise DeepFM harms standalone ranking and provides no trusted marginal portfolio gain. They do not establish that censored watch-time supervision is universally ineffective, because the result is specific to this parent reproduction, objective, auxiliary weight, and implementation; the supplied outcome also does not report the target-audit counters needed to independently verify masking and censoring correctness.
next_lesson: Do not reuse this fixed-weight watch auxiliary on w002; if revisited, isolate a much smaller auxiliary weight while retaining explicit masking and censoring audits.
